Events workbench

Source: R/workbench.R
event_workbench.Rd

A hydrologist calibrating by eye looks at the largest floods, changes a parameter, and looks again. event_workbench() sets that up for a calibration project: it finds the events in the registered record with find_events(), screens them with screen_events(), and keeps the n largest in the chosen window. workbench_try() reruns those events with some parameters changed and scores each one; plot_workbench() draws them side by side, before and after. The Events tab of calibration_app() puts the same on sliders, and saves a setting you accept as a logged trial.

Usage

event_workbench(
  project,
  entry = NULL,
  n = 10L,
  window = c("calibration", "validation", "all"),
  screen = list()
)

workbench_try(wb, changes)

plot_workbench(wb, trial = NULL, ncol = 2L)

Arguments

project

A calibration project folder.

entry

Id of the model entry to start from (structure, trial or calibration), or of a candidate, which stands for the entry it proposed. By default the latest candidate, or the latest model entry if there is none.

n

Number of events, largest observed peak first.

window

Window the events' peaks must lie in: calibration, validation or all.

screen

Settings for screen_events(); NULL keeps every event.

wb

A workbench from event_workbench().

changes

Named numeric vector of new parameter values by configuration path, such as c(surface.k1 = 3, td = 1.5), as for log_trial().

trial

A result of workbench_try() to draw beside the starting run.

ncol

Panels per row.

Value

event_workbench(): a pdm_workbench list with the project path, the starting entry (parent) and its configuration, the chosen events, the saved states, the starting run's flow in each event window (base) and its scores. workbench_try(): a list with the changed configuration, the flow in each window (runs), scores (one row per event: observed and simulated peak, peak error, timing error in hours and event NSE), and full_run, whether the whole record had to be rerun. plot_workbench(): wb, invisibly.

Details

Speed. A change to the surface stores or the time delay reruns only the event windows, from states saved just before each (event_states()), with a lead-in long enough for the slowest surface stores the bounds allow; that takes a fraction of a second. A change to anything else, such as the store shape b, alters the soil and groundwater stores before each event, so the whole record is rerun, which takes about a second for sixteen years of 15-minute data.

See also

calibration_app(), event_states(), screen_events(), log_trial()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
wb <- event_workbench("projects/beggearn_huish", n = 10)
faster <- workbench_try(wb, c(surface.k1 = 3, surface.k2 = 6, td = 1))
plot_workbench(wb, faster)
faster$scores
} # }
